title: Five works, four ways of looking

brief.title: An orchid, a distant forest
brief.angle: The change in scale between a suspended blossom and a distant forest.
brief.lead: The pale blossom fills the upper half of the painting. Below it, the forest recedes into smaller, darker marks.

notes.text: A large pale flower hangs above a small, dark forest.

brief.title: Lace against a dark dress
brief.angle: The patterned white collar forms a bright boundary between the face and the dark dress.
brief.lead: The wide collar spreads across the shoulders. Its pale loops stand out against the nearly black fabric below.

notes.heading: The scalloped edge
notes.text: Loops of white lace cross the dark fabric, with a small brooch at the centre.

brief.title: A hand beneath the tilted face
brief.angle: The tilted head and supporting hand create a diagonal above the child.
brief.lead: A hand supports the lowered face. Behind the two figures, small buildings and pale hills continue into the distance.

notes.text: The woman's head leans into her hand while the child's face turns outward.

brief.title: Two openings into the distance
brief.angle: Compare how a narrow wooded hollow and a broad stretch of water lead toward distant mountains.
brief.lead: Both landscapes place darker trees in front of pale mountains. The opening between them changes from a narrow hollow to a wide expanse of water.
brief.comparison_rationale: Gainsborough places a narrow wooded hollow beside a sloping rock; Duncanson opens the foreground around a broad stretch of water.

notes.text: Trees on the left and a sloping rock on the right frame a narrow wooded hollow.
Dark trees frame a broad stretch of water, with pale mountains extending behind it.
